summary: The revised manuscript resolves three open problems from Sharma et al. (arXiv:2611.34668v1) on discrete Wigner negativity and magic lower bounds in odd-dimensional qudit systems. It proves four original results: (1) a universal level-m Hankel-SOS quantitative bound recovering B3 at m=1, providing closed-form Schur-complement witnesses at m=2, and closing the blind zone of the physical ququint state rho2(p) down to p=0.45; (2) a signed-decomposition proof and exact equality characterization of the B3 inequality; (3) an explicit all-odd-dimension D >= 3 quasiprobability separation family x^(D) between (H1, B4) and H2-SOS; and (4) a reverse-monotonicity theorem via Holder's inequality proving k=2 (B4) is uniquely optimal among even-moment multiplicative mana bounds. Re-inspection of the updated PDF confirms all prior objections and minor errors are resolved: Remark 1 and the Verification Boundary explicitly prove x^(D) is non-realizable by any physical density matrix for odd prime D >= 3 (contrasting with rho2(p)), Theorem 1 item 2 correctly states v_Schur in R^3 (and Q^3 for rational moments), and Figure 1 Left / Figure 2 Right labels are accurate.
strengths: Theorem 1 upgrades Sharma et al.'s qualitative Hankel hierarchy (m >= 2) into explicit quantitative lower bounds on sum negativity and mana, recovering B3 identically as the optimal m=1 dual and systematically closing the rho2(p) blind zone (verified at p=0.60 with B3=2/959 and H2-SOS=1.264*B3, and at p=0.45 with H4-SOS=12393/2072994560000).

Theorem 4 settles the higher-even-moment generalization of B4 completely, proving multiplicativity and strict reverse-monotonicity (Lambda_4 > Lambda_6 > ...) whenever |W| is non-constant on its support.
Theorem 2 establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for exact saturation of (P-N)^2 <= (1+N)(b+N) alongside tighter signed-decomposition intermediates.

Remark 1 and the Verification Boundary transparently and accurately delineate quasiprobability separation (Theorem 3, unphysical for odd prime D >= 3) from physical-state separation (rho2(p) in C04-C08), and separate mechanized Lean 4.36.0 theorems from analytic proofs.
weaknesses: Mathematically, all four theorems rely on elementary techniques (a 4-line positivity/negativity split in Thm. 1, Cauchy-Schwarz plus quadratic expansion in Thm. 2, polynomial evaluation in Thm. 3, and two standard Holder applications in Thm. 4).

Theorem 3 constructs non-physical quasiprobabilities x^(D) for odd prime D >= 3 (as now explicitly noted in Remark 1), leaving physical density-matrix (H1, B4)-blind-spot families for arbitrary odd D >= 7 open.

Theorem 2 re-proves the inequality P^2 - b <= N(1 + 2P + b) already implicit in Sharma et al.'s Theorem 4 (since b >= -P implies 1+2P+b >= 1+P > 0 unconditionally), so its genuinely new mathematical content is the intermediate bound and equality characterization.
At higher Hankel levels m >= 3 (e.g., q4 at p=0.45 in C08), the method requires state-dependent ad hoc witness construction rather than a closed-form optimal dual.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 1: Universal level-m Hankel-SOS quantitative lower bound N(rho) >= max(0, -v^T H_m v)/M_v, its exact m=1 duality with B3, and deterministic H2 Schur-complement witnesses closing the rho2(p) blind zone.
Theorem 4: Generalized even-moment multiplicative mana family Lambda_{2k} and proof of strict reverse-monotonicity establishing k=2 as uniquely optimal.
